facts.statement: Janusaurus was an extinct genus of ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur.
facts.quote: Janusaurus is an extinct genus of ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur

facts.statement: Janusaurus fossils were found in the Upper Jurassic Slottsmøya Member of the Agardhfjellet Formation in Central Spitsbergen.
facts.quote: from the Upper Jurassic Slottsmøya Member, Agardhfjellet Formation of Central Spitsbergen

facts.statement: The holotype of Janusaurus consists of a partial skull and postcranial bones.
facts.quote: The holotype consists of a partial skull and postcrania

facts.statement: The individual represented by the holotype would have measured between 3 and 4 meters in length.
facts.quote: and would have belonged to an individual measuring 3 - 4 m long

facts.statement: In 2019, Nikolay Zverkov and Natalya Prilepskaya synonymized Janusaurus with Arthropterygius but kept it as a separate species.
facts.quote: In 2019, Janusaurus was synonymized with Arthropterygius, though maintained as a separate species, by Nikolay Zverkov and Natalya Prilepskaya

facts.statement: Janusaurus is classified within the family Ophthalmosauridae.
The genus Janusaurus was described by Roberts et al. in 2014.
The type species of the genus Janusaurus is Janusaurus lundi.
Janusaurus belongs to the subfamily Ophthalmosaurinae.

rejected.statement: Lene Delsett and colleagues objected to the 2019 synonymy, arguing that Janusaurus and Arthropterygius were different enough to warrant separate genera.
rejected.quote: although this synonymy was objected to later that same year by Lene Delsett and colleagues, who maintained that they were sufficiently different to warrant separate genera
